subject: Spain
note: Cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary): Antipodes on Earth (rev 1386178289), and the coordinates the API returns for Madrid, Weber (New Zealand), Whangārei, Tangier and Wellington (pinned revisions below). The antipode of a point is computed, not looked up: (latitude, longitude) becomes (-latitude, longitude ± 180°), as the page states; distances are on a sphere of radius 6,371 km. Computed claims say so. The page lists pairs of antipodal places (Madrid and Weber, Wellington and Alaejos, Auckland and Seville and Málaga, Whangārei and Tangier); the video uses only those and the two computed distances. The page's 15% figure is its cited source's estimate (another source on the page says about 3% of Earth's surface), so it is attributed and kept to the page's wording.

claims.text: The antipode of any place on Earth is the point diametrically opposite it; a straight line joining them passes through Earth's centre.
If a point's coordinates are (latitude, longitude), its antipode is at (-latitude, longitude ± 180°).
The antipodes of most of New Zealand's North Island lie in Spain.
Parts of Spain, Portugal, France and Morocco are antipodal to New Zealand.
The page lists antipodal pairs: Madrid and Weber (New Zealand); Wellington and Alaejos (Spain); Auckland and Seville and Málaga (Spain); Whangārei and Tangier (Morocco).
Most of the Earth's land surfaces have ocean at their antipodes, because most of the Earth's surface is covered in water.
Approximately 15% of land territory is antipodal to other land, according to the page's cited source.
The antipode of Madrid (40.4169° N, 3.7033° W, as given on its page) is at 40.4169° S, 176.2967° E, about 2 km from Weber, New Zealand (40.4014° S, 176.3111° E, as given on its page).
Madrid and Weber, New Zealand are 20,013 km apart on a sphere of radius 6,371 km; half the circumference of that sphere is 20,015 km.
The antipode of Whangārei (35.725° S, 174.3236° E) is about 13 km from Tangier (35.7767° N, 5.8039° W).
